fix.notes: The tile minimum width is no longer enforced (tiles can be narrower than 11rem on small screens), but this is intentional — at 2 columns on a 320 px screen each tile is ~160 px wide which is acceptable. Column breakpoints (500 px, 700 px, 1000 px) were chosen to keep tiles at a comfortable readable width at each step.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The `.metagame-grid` CSS used `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(11rem, 1fr))`, which lets the browser pick the column count automatically based on available space. When the number of archetype tiles isn't a multiple of that auto-computed count, the last row is partially filled — a "ragged end" where the final tiles stretch wider than intended.

## What changed

Replaced the single `auto-fit` rule with explicit `grid-template-columns` values at four `@media` breakpoints (`shared_web/static/css/pd.css`):

- Default (< 500 px): `repeat(2, 1fr)`
- ≥ 500 px: `repeat(3, 1fr)`
- ≥ 700 px: `repeat(4, 1fr)`
- ≥ 1000 px: `repeat(6, 1fr)`

All four column counts (2, 3, 4, 6) are factors of 24 — the maximum number of metagame archetypes displayed — so the grid will always be evenly divisible and the last row never appears ragged.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks passed)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped in 15.80 s

Fixes #12563
fix.pr_title: Fix metagame grid ragged end by using factor-of-24 column counts (#12563)

Issue author suggests 'disallow 5 and 7 tile wide in css somehow' — CSS media queries with specific column counts (e.g. 2, 3, 4, 6) would prevent non-factor-of-24 widths
